questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Physical Education is best defined as an educational process that primarily uses
options: physical activity as a means to develop the total fitness and well-being of an individual
only theoretical study of sports history with no practical activity
purely academic classroom instruction with no physical activity
only competitive professional sports training
questions.explanation: Physical Education uses purposeful physical activity as an educational tool to develop the physical, mental, social, and emotional well-being of individuals.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following is a recognised general aim of Physical Education?
options: Discouraging any form of physical activity
Eliminating team sports from the curriculum
Promoting physical fitness, health, and the development of motor skills
Focusing exclusively on producing professional athletes
questions.explanation: A core aim of Physical Education is to promote overall physical fitness, health, and the development of fundamental motor skills, benefiting all participants, not just aspiring professional athletes.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Recreation, as it relates to Physical Education, refers to
options: medical treatment for sports injuries
purely academic study with no physical component
activities pursued during leisure time for enjoyment, relaxation, and personal fulfilment
mandatory competitive sports training with no leisure element
questions.explanation: Recreation encompasses activities people choose to engage in during their free time for enjoyment, relaxation, and personal satisfaction, often incorporating physical activity.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following is a recognised career pathway within the field of Physical Education and sports?
options: Accounting
Pharmacy
Civil engineering
Sports coaching
questions.explanation: Sports coaching is a well-established career pathway within Physical Education, alongside other options such as sports administration, physiotherapy, and PE teaching.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The history of organised Physical Education is often traced back significantly to the practices of
options: ancient Greece, particularly through the Olympic Games
purely indoor academic study with no physical activity
modern 21st-century fitness trends exclusively
only 20th-century professional sports leagues
questions.explanation: Ancient Greek civilisation, notably through the ancient Olympic Games, is widely regarded as a foundational historical influence on the development of organised physical education and competitive sport.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best describes an objective of Physical Education related to social development?
options: Fostering teamwork, cooperation, and fair play through group physical activities
Encouraging students to avoid all interaction with peers
Discouraging sportsmanship and fair competition
Focusing exclusively on individual, solitary activities with no team component
questions.explanation: A key social objective of Physical Education is to develop important interpersonal skills such as teamwork, cooperation, and fair play, often cultivated through group and team-based physical activities.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Sprint events in track athletics typically cover distances of
options: 10km, half-marathon, and marathon distances
only distances beyond 10,000m
questions.explanation: Sprint events are short-distance races, typically covering 100m, 200m, and 400m, requiring maximum speed over a relatively brief duration.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Middle-distance events in track athletics typically include races such as
options: 800m and 1500m
the marathon (42.195km)
the long jump and high jump
100m and 200m sprints
questions.explanation: Middle-distance races, such as the 800m and 1500m, require a combination of speed and endurance, positioned between short sprints and longer distance events.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Long-distance events in track athletics typically include races such as
options: the 400m hurdles
5000m, 10,000m, and the marathon
100m and 200m sprints
the 4x100m relay
questions.explanation: Long-distance track and road events, such as the 5000m, 10,000m, and marathon, primarily test an athlete's aerobic endurance over extended distances.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Hurdles, a track event in athletics, require athletes to
options: run a set distance while jumping over a series of fixed barriers
throw a heavy metal ball as far as possible
jump over a bar set at increasing heights
pass a baton to teammates in sequence
questions.explanation: Hurdle races require athletes to sprint a specified distance while clearing a series of evenly spaced barriers (hurdles) without knocking them down.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In relay races, an important element of track athletics, competitors must
options: jump over a series of hurdles individually
throw an implement rather than run
complete the entire race individually with no baton exchange
pass a baton to the next teammate within a designated exchange zone
questions.explanation: Relay races require team members to successfully pass a baton to the next runner within a specifically marked exchange zone, with the race disqualified if the exchange occurs outside this zone.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The standard distance of the 4x100m relay refers to
options: four athletes running 100m simultaneously side by side with no baton exchange
four separate races of 100m each scored independently
a single athlete running 400m alone
four athletes each running 100m, for a total combined distance of 400m
questions.explanation: The 4x100m relay involves a team of four athletes, each running a 100m leg and passing the baton to the next teammate, for a total combined race distance of 400m.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A false start in a track race occurs when
options: a runner finishes the race in first place
a runner leaves the starting blocks before the starting signal is given
a runner clears a hurdle successfully
a runner successfully passes the baton in a relay
questions.explanation: A false start occurs when an athlete begins moving from the starting blocks before the official starting signal (gun or similar) is given, which can result in disqualification under current rules.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which official in track athletics is primarily responsible for determining the order in which runners finish a race?
options: The starter
The timekeeper exclusively, with no role in determining placing
The judge (or photo-finish official)
The groundskeeper
questions.explanation: Judges (often assisted by photo-finish technology) are responsible for determining the precise finishing order of competitors in a track race.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The long jump, a field event in athletics, requires athletes to
options: jump over a horizontal bar for maximum height
throw a heavy implement for maximum distance
sprint down a runway and jump for maximum horizontal distance into a sand pit
run a fixed distance as quickly as possible
questions.explanation: In the long jump, athletes sprint along a runway before jumping from a take-off board, aiming to achieve the maximum horizontal distance before landing in a sand pit.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The high jump, a field event in athletics, requires athletes to
options: jump over a horizontal bar set at increasing heights without knocking it down
jump for maximum horizontal distance
sprint a fixed distance
throw an implement for maximum distance
questions.explanation: In the high jump, athletes attempt to clear a horizontal bar set at progressively increasing heights, with the winner being the athlete who clears the greatest height without dislodging the bar.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The triple jump, a field event in athletics, is characterised by a sequence of
options: throwing an implement three times in succession
a hop, a step, and a jump, performed in a single continuous motion
a single maximal jump only
three separate identical jumps with rest in between
questions.explanation: The triple jump requires athletes to perform a specific sequence of a hop, a step, and a final jump in one continuous, fluid motion, aiming for maximum combined horizontal distance.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The shot put, a throwing field event in athletics, requires athletes to
options: jump over a horizontal bar
throw a discus-shaped implement using a spinning technique
push (rather than throw with a swinging motion) a heavy spherical metal ball for maximum distance
throw a javelin using a running approach
questions.explanation: The shot put requires athletes to 'put' (push) a heavy spherical metal ball from the shoulder, rather than throwing it with a swinging arm motion, aiming for maximum distance.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The discus throw, a field event in athletics, involves athletes
options: jumping over a bar set at increasing heights
running with a javelin before releasing it
pushing a heavy spherical ball from the shoulder
spinning within a circle before releasing a flat, disc-shaped implement for maximum distance
questions.explanation: The discus throw involves athletes performing a rotational spinning technique within a throwing circle before releasing the flat, disc-shaped implement for maximum distance.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The javelin throw, a field event in athletics, involves athletes
options: spinning within a circle before releasing a discus
jumping into a sand pit for maximum distance
running along an approach runway before throwing a spear-like implement for maximum distance
pushing a heavy ball from the shoulder
questions.explanation: The javelin throw requires athletes to build speed along a running approach before releasing the spear-like javelin implement, aiming for maximum throwing distance.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In football (soccer), a standard match is officiated primarily by
options: a single umpire with no assistants
a referee, assisted by assistant referees (linesmen)
a scorekeeper with no on-field authority
a panel of judges scoring style points
questions.explanation: Football matches are officiated by a central referee, who has ultimate authority over the game, assisted by assistant referees (linesmen) who help monitor the sidelines, offside calls, and other aspects of play.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In football, an offside offence generally occurs when an attacking player is
options: nearer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender when the ball is played to them
taking a corner kick
positioned anywhere on their own half of the pitch
in possession of the ball inside their own penalty area
questions.explanation: The offside rule in football penalises an attacking player who is nearer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender at the moment the ball is played to them, subject to specific exceptions.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In basketball, a standard game is typically divided into
options: innings, similar to baseball
four quarters
three periods
two halves only, with no quarters
questions.explanation: Standard basketball games (such as under FIBA or NBA rules) are typically divided into four quarters, though specific quarter lengths can vary between different competition levels and organisations.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In basketball, a 'travelling' violation occurs when a player
options: takes an illegal number of steps while holding the ball without dribbling
successfully makes a three-point shot
passes the ball to a teammate legally
commits a foul against an opposing player
questions.explanation: Travelling is a basketball violation that occurs when a player holding the ball takes an excessive number of steps without dribbling it, resulting in a turnover to the opposing team.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In volleyball, a team is generally allowed a maximum of how many touches to return the ball across the net (not counting a block)?
options: One touch only
Unlimited touches
Five touches
Three touches
questions.explanation: In standard volleyball rules, a team is permitted a maximum of three touches (not including a block contact) to return the ball successfully over the net to the opposing side.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In volleyball, which skill is primarily used to initiate play at the start of each rally?
options: The set
The serve
The block
The dig
questions.explanation: The serve is the skill used to put the ball into play at the beginning of each rally in volleyball, typically performed from behind the back boundary line.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In handball, players are generally permitted to hold the ball for a maximum of how many seconds before passing, dribbling, or shooting?
options: One minute
There is no time limit at all
Thirty seconds
Three seconds
questions.explanation: Handball rules typically limit players to holding the ball for a maximum of three seconds without dribbling, passing, or shooting, encouraging fast-paced play.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In hockey (field hockey), players use which part of the stick to legally play the ball?
options: Only the rounded (back) side of the stick
Any part of the body other than the stick
Only the flat side of the stick
Either side of the stick, flat or rounded
questions.explanation: Field hockey rules require players to play the ball using only the flat side of the stick; using the rounded back side to strike the ball is an infringement.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In cricket, a standard team consists of how many players on the field at one time?
options: Six players
Fifteen players
Eleven players
Nine players
questions.explanation: A standard cricket team fields eleven players at any given time, following the traditional format of the game.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In cricket, a batsman is given 'out' via a 'bowled' dismissal when
options: the batsman scores a boundary (four or six runs)
the batsman successfully completes a run
the fielding team appeals unsuccessfully
the bowler's delivery hits and dislodges the bails from the batsman's wicket
questions.explanation: A 'bowled' dismissal in cricket occurs when the bowler's delivery directly strikes the batsman's wicket and dislodges the bails, resulting in the batsman being given out.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In tennis, a standard singles match is generally won by a player who wins
options: the majority of sets, typically best-of-three or best-of-five sets depending on the competition
a single point only
exactly one game with no further requirement
the coin toss before the match begins
questions.explanation: Tennis matches are generally decided by winning the majority of sets played, commonly in a best-of-three format for most competitions, or best-of-five in some major men's tournaments.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In badminton, players use a racket to strike which type of projectile?
options: A hockey ball
A shuttlecock
A tennis ball
A table tennis ball
questions.explanation: Badminton is played using a lightweight shuttlecock, struck with a racket, distinguishing it from tennis (ball) and other racket sports.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In table tennis, players must allow the ball to bounce how many times on their side of the table before returning it, under normal rally conditions?
options: Exactly once
Not at all, it must be volleyed directly
Twice
Three times
questions.explanation: Under standard table tennis rules, the ball must bounce exactly once on a player's side of the table before they legally return it to the opponent's side.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In basketball, a successful shot made from beyond the designated arc is awarded how many points?
options: Two points, the same as any other shot
One point
Five points
Three points
questions.explanation: A successful field goal made from beyond the three-point arc in basketball is awarded three points, compared to two points for shots made inside the arc.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Floor activities, a component of gymnastics, are typically performed
options: on a padded mat, involving a sequence of tumbling and balance movements without additional apparatus
exclusively on a raised balance beam
exclusively using a vaulting box
exclusively on parallel bars
questions.explanation: Floor exercises in gymnastics are performed on a padded mat, combining tumbling, balance, and flexibility movements without the use of additional apparatus.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The vaulting box, a piece of gymnastics apparatus, is primarily used for
options: balance beam routines exclusively
performing vaulting movements, where an athlete runs, springs off a board, and executes movements over the box
floor tumbling exclusively
rhythmic ribbon exercises exclusively
questions.explanation: The vaulting box (or vaulting horse/table) is used for vaulting exercises, in which an athlete sprints toward the apparatus, springs off a springboard, and performs specific movements while passing over it.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Parallel bars, a piece of apparatus used in artistic gymnastics, primarily require athletes to
options: run and jump over a raised bar
throw an implement for distance
perform swinging, balancing, and strength movements while supporting themselves between two raised, parallel bars
perform floor tumbling exclusively
questions.explanation: Parallel bars require gymnasts to perform a sequence of swinging, balancing, and strength-based movements while supporting their body weight between two raised, parallel horizontal bars.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Rhythmic gymnastics is particularly distinguished from artistic gymnastics by its incorporation of
options: exclusive use of parallel bars
handheld apparatus such as ribbons, hoops, and balls, combined with dance-like movements
the complete absence of any music accompaniment
exclusive use of the vaulting box
questions.explanation: Rhythmic gymnastics distinctively incorporates handheld apparatus, such as ribbons, hoops, balls, and clubs, combined with expressive, dance-like movements, typically performed to music.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Traditional folk dances, an important component of dance within Physical Education, are generally characterised by
options: steps identical across all cultures worldwide with no local variation
movements and steps rooted in the cultural traditions and history of a particular community
movements exclusively performed using gymnastics apparatus
purely modern, internationally standardised dance steps with no cultural connection
questions.explanation: Traditional folk dances reflect and preserve the specific cultural heritage, customs, and history of the particular community or region from which they originate.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best describes a key physical benefit of participating in gymnastics and dance activities?
options: Improved flexibility, balance, coordination, and overall body control
Decreased overall physical fitness
No measurable physical benefit whatsoever
Exclusive development of upper body strength with no other benefit
questions.explanation: Regular participation in gymnastics and dance activities helps develop important physical attributes, including flexibility, balance, coordination, and overall body control.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Long bones, a type of bone found in the human skeletal system, are typically found in locations such as the
options: vertebrae exclusively
wrist and ankle exclusively
arms and legs (e.g., the femur and humerus)
skull
questions.explanation: Long bones, characterised by their length exceeding their width, are typically found in the limbs, such as the femur (thigh bone) and humerus (upper arm bone).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Short bones, a type of bone found in the human skeletal system, are typically found in locations such as the
options: skull
ribs
wrist (carpals) and ankle (tarsals)
arms and legs
questions.explanation: Short bones are roughly cube-shaped and are typically found in areas requiring stability and limited movement, such as the carpal bones of the wrist and tarsal bones of the ankle.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Flat bones, a type of bone found in the human skeletal system, are typically found in locations such as the
options: fingers and toes
skull and ribs
wrist and ankle
upper arm and thigh
questions.explanation: Flat bones, characterised by their thin, often curved shape, are typically found in areas requiring protection of internal organs, such as the skull (protecting the brain) and the ribs (protecting the chest cavity).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A ball-and-socket joint, a type of joint in the human body, permits movement
options: in only one plane, like a door hinge
only in a rotating motion around a single axis
with almost no movement at all
in almost all directions, as seen at the shoulder and hip
questions.explanation: A ball-and-socket joint, where a rounded bone head fits into a cup-like socket, allows the widest range of movement of any joint type, as seen at the shoulder and hip.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A hinge joint, a type of joint in the human body, permits movement
options: with no movement at all
in all directions, as seen at the shoulder
in one plane only, similar to a door hinge, as seen at the elbow and knee
only a gliding motion between flat bone surfaces
questions.explanation: A hinge joint allows movement (flexion and extension) in a single plane, similar to the mechanical action of a door hinge, as seen at the elbow and knee joints.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Flexion, a type of joint movement, refers to
options: moving a limb away from the midline of the body
rotating a limb around its own axis
increasing the angle between two body parts at a joint
decreasing the angle between two body parts at a joint, such as bending the elbow
questions.explanation: Flexion describes a joint movement that decreases the angle between connected body segments, such as bending the arm at the elbow.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Extension, a type of joint movement, refers to
options: decreasing the angle between two body parts at a joint
moving a limb toward the midline of the body
rotating a limb around its own axis
increasing the angle between two body parts at a joint, such as straightening the elbow
questions.explanation: Extension describes a joint movement that increases the angle between connected body segments, such as straightening a previously bent arm at the elbow, the opposite of flexion.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Abduction, a type of joint movement, refers to
options: moving a limb or body part toward the midline of the body
decreasing the angle at a joint
rotating a limb around its own axis
moving a limb or body part away from the midline of the body
questions.explanation: Abduction describes a movement that takes a limb or body part away from the central midline of the body, such as raising an arm out to the side.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Skeletal (voluntary) muscles, a type of muscle in the human body, are characterised by being
options: incapable of contracting or producing any movement
under entirely involuntary control, such as the heart muscle
found exclusively within the walls of internal organs
under conscious, voluntary control, and typically attached to bones to produce movement
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscles are voluntary muscles, meaning they can be consciously controlled, and are typically attached to bones via tendons, enabling deliberate body movement.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Regular exercise generally affects skeletal muscle fibres by
options: increasing their size (hypertrophy) and improving their strength and endurance capacity
converting all muscle fibres into bone tissue
causing them to permanently shrink and weaken
having no measurable effect on muscle tissue whatsoever
questions.explanation: Consistent exercise, particularly resistance training, generally leads to muscle fibre hypertrophy (increased size) and improved overall strength and endurance capacity.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a joint movement classified as rotation?
options: Turning the head from side to side
Straightening the elbow
Raising the arm out to the side
Bending the knee
questions.explanation: Rotation describes a joint movement in which a body part turns around its own longitudinal axis, such as turning the head from side to side at the neck.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The human heart is best described as a
options: component of the digestive system
purely passive storage organ for blood with no pumping function
structure responsible for filtering air in the lungs
muscular pump responsible for circulating blood throughout the body
questions.explanation: The heart is a powerful, muscular organ that rhythmically contracts to pump blood throughout the circulatory system, delivering oxygen and nutrients to body tissues.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The human heart consists of how many main chambers?
options: Six chambers
Two chambers only
Three chambers only
Four (two atria and two ventricles)
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two upper chambers (the left and right atria) and two lower chambers (the left and right ventricles).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Oxygenated blood, pumped from the left ventricle of the heart, is transported throughout the body primarily via the
options: pulmonary veins exclusively
aorta and systemic arteries
vena cava exclusively
pulmonary artery exclusively
questions.explanation: Oxygen-rich blood leaves the heart's left ventricle via the aorta, the body's largest artery, which branches into systemic arteries supplying oxygenated blood throughout the body.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Deoxygenated blood returning from the body to the heart enters primarily through the
options: vena cava, into the right atrium
pulmonary veins, into the left atrium
aorta, into the left ventricle
coronary arteries exclusively
questions.explanation: Deoxygenated blood returning from body tissues enters the heart's right atrium via the vena cava (the superior and inferior vena cava), before being pumped onward to the lungs for reoxygenation.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Breathing (respiration mechanics) involves the coordinated action primarily of the
options: digestive system muscles
skeletal muscles of the arms exclusively
diaphragm and intercostal muscles
heart muscle exclusively
questions.explanation: Breathing mechanics rely on the coordinated contraction and relaxation of the diaphragm (a large muscle beneath the lungs) and the intercostal muscles between the ribs, changing the volume of the chest cavity.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: During inhalation, the diaphragm generally
options: has no role in the breathing process
relaxes and domes upward, decreasing chest cavity volume
contracts and flattens, increasing the volume of the chest cavity to draw air into the lungs
stops moving entirely
questions.explanation: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and moves downward, flattening its dome shape and increasing the volume of the chest cavity, which draws air into the lungs.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Oxygen debt, a physiological concept in exercise science, refers to
options: the additional oxygen the body requires after strenuous exercise to restore normal metabolic conditions
a permanent, irreversible reduction in lung capacity
the complete absence of any oxygen in the bloodstream
the total amount of oxygen inhaled during a single breath
questions.explanation: Oxygen debt refers to the extra oxygen consumption needed after intense exercise to help the body recover, replenish energy stores, and clear metabolic by-products such as lactic acid.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Aerobic exercise is characterised by activities that are
options: performed at a moderate intensity over a sustained period, primarily using oxygen to produce energy
performed without any cardiovascular involvement whatsoever
purely stationary with no movement involved
extremely short and intense, relying on energy production without oxygen
questions.explanation: Aerobic exercise involves sustained, moderate-intensity activity (such as jogging or swimming) in which the body primarily uses oxygen to generate the energy needed for continued effort.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Anaerobic exercise is characterised by activities that are
options: always performed for durations exceeding one hour
long, sustained, moderate-intensity efforts using oxygen throughout
short, intense bursts of effort, where energy is produced without sufficient oxygen supply
purely passive with no muscular exertion
questions.explanation: Anaerobic exercise involves brief, high-intensity bursts of effort (such as sprinting or heavy weightlifting), during which the body's energy demands exceed the available oxygen supply, relying on alternative energy pathways.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the difference between aerobic and anaerobic exercise?
options: Both long-distance running and 100m sprints are identical in their energy production
Long-distance running is anaerobic, while sprinting is aerobic
Long-distance running is primarily aerobic, while a 100m sprint is primarily anaerobic
Neither activity involves any form of energy production
questions.explanation: Long-distance running relies primarily on sustained aerobic (oxygen-based) energy production, while a short, maximal-effort 100m sprint relies primarily on rapid anaerobic energy pathways.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Regular cardiovascular (aerobic) exercise generally has which effect on the heart over time?
options: It has no effect whatsoever on cardiovascular function
It can strengthen the heart muscle, improving its efficiency in pumping blood
It permanently weakens the heart muscle
It stops the heart from beating regularly
questions.explanation: Consistent aerobic exercise training generally strengthens the heart muscle over time, improving its pumping efficiency and overall cardiovascular fitness.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A sprain, a common sports injury, refers to
options: an injury to a ligament, typically caused by overstretching or tearing
a break in a bone
a break in the skin causing bleeding
an injury to a muscle or tendon
questions.explanation: A sprain specifically involves damage to a ligament (the connective tissue linking bones at a joint), typically from overstretching or partial/complete tearing due to sudden twisting or impact.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A strain, a common sports injury, refers to
options: a break in a bone
a dislocation of a joint
an injury to a ligament specifically
an injury to a muscle or tendon, typically caused by overstretching or overexertion
questions.explanation: A strain involves damage to a muscle or tendon, often resulting from overstretching, overexertion, or sudden excessive force during physical activity.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A dislocation, a sports injury affecting a joint, occurs when
options: the skin is cut, causing bleeding
a muscle is torn or overstretched
the bones forming a joint are forced out of their normal alignment
a ligament is overstretched without bone displacement
questions.explanation: A dislocation occurs when the bones that form a joint are displaced from their normal anatomical position, often requiring prompt medical attention to safely realign them.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A fracture, a serious injury affecting bone, refers to
options: a minor bruise with no bone involvement
a break or crack in a bone
an injury limited to a muscle only
an injury limited to a ligament only
questions.explanation: A fracture specifically refers to a break, crack, or other structural disruption of a bone, ranging in severity from a hairline crack to a complete break.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A muscle cramp, a common exercise-related condition, is best described as
options: a permanent loss of muscle function
a break in the bone underlying the muscle
a type of skin injury causing bleeding
a sudden, involuntary, and often painful muscle contraction
questions.explanation: A muscle cramp is a sudden, involuntary, and often painful contraction of a muscle, which can occur during or after physical exertion, sometimes related to fatigue, dehydration, or electrolyte imbalance.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: When managing external bleeding as a first aid measure, the initial recommended action is generally to
options: apply direct, firm pressure to the wound using a clean cloth or dressing
vigorously massage the surrounding area
immediately remove any embedded object from the wound
submerge the wound in cold water for an extended period
questions.explanation: Applying direct, firm pressure to a bleeding wound with a clean cloth or dressing is a fundamental first aid technique to help control and reduce blood loss.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is an emergency procedure primarily used when a person
options: has a common cold
is not breathing and has no detectable pulse, to help maintain blood circulation and oxygen delivery
has a mild muscle cramp
has a minor cut requiring a simple bandage
questions.explanation: CPR is a critical emergency procedure performed when someone's breathing and heartbeat have stopped, using chest compressions (and often rescue breaths) to manually maintain blood circulation and oxygen delivery until further medical help arrives.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The R.I.C.E. method (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) is a common first aid approach primarily used for managing
options: soft tissue injuries such as sprains and strains
common respiratory infections
severe open fractures requiring surgery
cardiac arrest requiring CPR
questions.explanation: The R.I.C.E. method is a widely recommended initial first aid approach for managing soft tissue injuries like sprains and strains, helping to reduce pain, swelling, and further tissue damage.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A balanced diet is best described as one that
options: eliminates all forms of carbohydrates entirely
provides all the essential nutrients in appropriate proportions needed for good health
consists of only a single type of food eaten exclusively
contains excessive amounts of sugar and fat with no other nutrients
questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies all essential nutrient classes (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water) in the correct proportions needed to maintain good health.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Carbohydrates, a major class of food nutrients, primarily function to
options: provide essential fatty acids exclusively
build and repair body tissues, as the primary function
provide the body's main and most readily available source of energy
regulate body processes as the primary function, like a hormone
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates serve as the body's primary and most readily accessible source of energy, fuelling everyday physical and mental activity.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Proteins, a major class of food nutrients, primarily function to
options: provide bulk (fibre) to aid digestion, as their primary function
serve as the body's primary and most readily available energy source
supply essential vitamins exclusively
build, repair, and maintain body tissues
questions.explanation: Proteins are essential for building, repairing, and maintaining body tissues, including muscles, and also play roles in enzyme and hormone production.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Fats (lipids), a major class of food nutrients, primarily function to
options: regulate blood sugar levels as their primary function
provide the body's primary source of dietary fibre
provide a concentrated source of energy and support the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins
build muscle tissue as their primary function
questions.explanation: Fats provide a highly concentrated source of energy and are necessary for the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K), among other important physiological functions.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Vitamins, a class of essential nutrients required in small amounts, primarily function to
options: serve as the body's primary source of energy
provide the majority of the body's caloric intake
build significant amounts of muscle tissue
regulate various body processes and support overall metabolic function
questions.explanation: Vitamins are required in relatively small quantities but play essential roles in regulating numerous body processes and supporting overall metabolic health.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Minerals, a class of essential nutrients, are important for functions such as
options: providing the majority of the body's dietary fibre
bone development (calcium) and oxygen transport in the blood (iron)
serving as the body's primary source of energy
regulating body temperature exclusively
questions.explanation: Minerals serve various essential physiological roles, such as calcium supporting bone development and strength, and iron being essential for oxygen transport within red blood cells.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Water, though not a traditional 'food' nutrient, is essential for the body mainly because it
options: provides significant caloric energy
is only needed in very small, negligible amounts
regulates body temperature, transports nutrients, and supports numerous vital physiological processes
builds muscle tissue directly
questions.explanation: Water is essential for regulating body temperature, transporting nutrients and waste products, and supporting virtually all vital physiological processes, despite providing no caloric energy itself.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: An eating disorder, a serious health condition related to nutrition, is best described as
options: a condition that has no impact on physical health
a temporary, harmless change in appetite
simply a strong personal preference for a particular type of food
a psychological condition characterised by abnormal or disturbed eating habits that negatively affect health
questions.explanation: Eating disorders are serious psychological conditions involving abnormal or disturbed eating patterns (such as anorexia nervosa or bulimia) that can significantly harm physical and mental health.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Anorexia nervosa, an example of an eating disorder, is generally characterised by
options: excessive, uncontrolled overeating with no associated distress
a purely physical condition with no psychological component
a complete absence of any body image concerns
severe restriction of food intake, often driven by an intense fear of gaining weight
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is characterised by severely restricted food intake, often driven by an intense fear of weight gain and a distorted perception of body image.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best represents general dietary advice for maintaining good personal health?
options: Eating only one type of food exclusively for extended periods
Consuming a varied, balanced diet alongside adequate hydration and regular physical activity
Completely eliminating all classes of nutrients from the diet
Avoiding water intake as much as possible
questions.explanation: Maintaining good personal health is generally best supported by a varied and balanced diet, adequate hydration, and regular physical activity, working together to support overall well-being.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Malaria, a communicable disease of significant concern in Nigeria, is primarily transmitted through
options: airborne respiratory droplets
the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito
contaminated water sources exclusively
direct person-to-person contact
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted to humans through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, making mosquito control a key prevention strategy.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: HIV/AIDS, a significant communicable disease, is primarily transmitted through
options: airborne respiratory droplets, similar to the common cold
contact with infected bodily fluids, such as blood or through unprotected sexual contact
casual social contact, such as shaking hands
contaminated food alone
questions.explanation: HIV is primarily transmitted through contact with certain infected bodily fluids, notably through unprotected sexual contact, sharing contaminated needles, or from mother to child during childbirth or breastfeeding.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Tuberculosis (TB), a significant communicable disease, primarily affects which part of the body?
options: Exclusively the skin
The lungs, though it can also affect other organs
Exclusively the digestive system
Exclusively the bones
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs, though it can also spread to and affect other organs in more severe cases.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Tuberculosis is primarily transmitted between people through
options: direct skin contact alone
insect bites
contaminated water sources
airborne respiratory droplets, such as from coughing or sneezing
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis spreads primarily through airborne respiratory droplets released when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or speaks, making it a highly contagious airborne disease.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Cholera, a significant communicable disease, is primarily transmitted through
options: airborne respiratory droplets
consumption of water or food contaminated with the cholera bacterium
direct skin-to-skin contact alone
insect bites
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by ingesting water or food contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, making safe water supply and sanitation crucial for prevention.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: COVID-19, a significant communicable disease, is primarily transmitted through
options: contaminated water sources exclusively
genetic inheritance from parents
respiratory droplets and aerosols released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes
insect bites exclusively
questions.explanation: COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, spreads primarily through respiratory droplets and aerosols released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following is a recommended general prevention measure against communicable respiratory diseases such as tuberculosis and COVID-19?
options: Practising good respiratory hygiene, such as covering coughs and sneezes
Deliberately sharing personal items with infected individuals
Avoiding all forms of vaccination
Ignoring any recommended public health guidelines
questions.explanation: Good respiratory hygiene practices, such as covering coughs and sneezes and practising proper hand hygiene, are important general measures for reducing the spread of airborne communicable diseases.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Hypertension (high blood pressure), a significant non-communicable disease, refers to a condition in which
options: red blood cell shape becomes abnormally sickle-shaped
blood sugar levels are consistently too low
the force of blood against artery walls is consistently too high
abnormal cell growth forms a malignant tumour
questions.explanation: Hypertension is a chronic condition characterised by persistently elevated blood pressure, which can increase the risk of serious complications such as heart disease and stroke if left unmanaged.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Diabetes, a significant non-communicable disease, is primarily characterised by
options: an infection caused by a virus
an infection caused by a bacterium
the body's inability to properly regulate blood glucose (sugar) levels
an abnormally low blood pressure
questions.explanation: Diabetes is a chronic metabolic condition in which the body cannot effectively regulate blood glucose levels, either due to insufficient insulin production or ineffective insulin use.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Cancer, a significant non-communicable disease, is generally characterised by
options: the uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells within the body
a bacterial infection of the respiratory system
a temporary and easily reversible imbalance in blood pressure
a viral infection transmitted through mosquito bites
questions.explanation: Cancer is fundamentally characterised by the uncontrolled growth and potential spread of abnormal cells, which can disrupt normal body function and, in some cases, spread to other parts of the body.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Sickle Cell Anaemia, a significant genetically inherited non-communicable disease particularly prevalent in Nigeria, is characterised by
options: a condition caused exclusively by poor diet
red blood cells taking on an abnormal, rigid, sickle (crescent) shape
a bacterial infection of the lungs
an infection caused by a mosquito-borne parasite
questions.explanation: Sickle Cell Anaemia is a genetically inherited blood disorder in which red blood cells become abnormally rigid and sickle (crescent) shaped, impairing their ability to carry oxygen efficiently and causing various health complications.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes a communicable disease from a non-communicable disease?
options: A communicable disease can be transmitted from person to person (or via a vector), while a non-communicable disease generally cannot
Both types of disease are always transmitted in exactly the same way
There is no meaningful distinction between the two categories
A non-communicable disease can be transmitted from person to person, while a communicable disease cannot
questions.explanation: The fundamental distinction lies in transmissibility: communicable diseases can spread between individuals (directly, or via a vector like a mosquito), whereas non-communicable diseases (like hypertension or diabetes) generally arise from other factors, such as genetics or lifestyle, and cannot be 'caught' from another person.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Alcohol abuse, a significant substance abuse concern, can lead to health effects including
options: no significant health risks whatsoever
liver damage and impaired cognitive and motor function
enhanced athletic performance with no negative effects
improved liver function over time
questions.explanation: Chronic alcohol abuse is associated with serious health consequences, including liver damage (such as cirrhosis) and impaired cognitive and motor functioning.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Tobacco use, a significant substance abuse concern, is particularly associated with an increased risk of
options: improved lung capacity and cardiovascular health
no significant long-term health consequences
lung cancer and various respiratory and cardiovascular diseases
enhanced athletic performance with no health risks
questions.explanation: Tobacco use is a well-established major risk factor for lung cancer and a range of other serious respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Narcotics, a category of drugs subject to abuse, are generally characterised by their
options: role as an essential daily nutrient
complete safety with no risk of dependency or harm
exclusive use as performance-enhancing supplements
potential to cause dependency and significantly impair physical and mental functioning
questions.explanation: Narcotic drugs, when abused, carry a significant risk of dependency (addiction) and can severely impair both physical health and mental/cognitive functioning.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Performance-enhancing drugs (doping), when used by athletes, are generally prohibited in competitive sport mainly because they
options: provide an unfair advantage and can pose serious risks to the athlete's health
are required by international sports regulations
have no effect whatsoever on athletic performance
are completely safe and universally permitted in all competitions
questions.explanation: Performance-enhancing drugs are banned in competitive sport primarily because they create an unfair competitive advantage and often carry significant risks to the athlete's long-term health.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The use of performance-enhancing drugs (doping) in sport can result in which of the following consequences for an athlete's career?
options: An automatic upgrade in competition ranking
Automatic guaranteed victory with no possible penalty
No consequences whatsoever, even if detected
Disqualification, suspension, or a permanent ban from competition if detected
questions.explanation: Athletes found to have used banned performance-enhancing substances typically face serious sporting sanctions, including disqualification from results, suspension, or even a permanent ban from competition.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best describes a general strategy for preventing drug and substance abuse, particularly among young people?
options: Providing no information at all about the risks involved
Actively promoting the use of performance-enhancing drugs in youth sports
Encouraging early and unrestricted exposure to addictive substances
Education about the risks and harmful effects of drug and substance abuse
questions.explanation: Providing clear, accurate education about the risks and harmful effects of drug and substance abuse is a widely recognised and important preventive strategy, particularly for young people.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A safe and reliable water supply is important for community health mainly because it helps
options: increase the spread of airborne respiratory diseases
cause an increase in non-communicable diseases exclusively
have no meaningful impact on public health
prevent waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid
questions.explanation: Access to safe, clean water is essential for preventing waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid, which spread through contaminated water sources.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Proper waste disposal systems are important for community health mainly because they help
options: increase the breeding of disease-carrying pests and organisms
have no impact on public health whatsoever
are only relevant to industrial factories, not residential communities
prevent the spread of disease-causing organisms and reduce environmental contamination
questions.explanation: Effective waste disposal systems help prevent the accumulation of waste that can breed disease-carrying pests and contaminate the environment, protecting overall community health.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Pollution control measures are important for community health mainly because they help
options: reduce harmful exposure to contaminated air, water, and soil
have no relevance to human health outcomes
increase the concentration of harmful pollutants in the environment
exclusively benefit wildlife with no impact on human communities
questions.explanation: Pollution control measures aim to limit the release of harmful substances into the air, water, and soil, directly reducing human exposure to environmental health hazards.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The World Health Organization (WHO), an important international health agency, is primarily responsible for
options: regulating the food and drug industries of a single specific country
manufacturing pharmaceutical products for individual countries
providing direct primary healthcare exclusively within Nigeria
coordinating international public health efforts and providing global health guidance
questions.explanation: The WHO is a specialised United Nations agency responsible for coordinating international public health initiatives and providing global guidance and leadership on health matters.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which distinction most accurately separates the 'narrow' traditional view of Physical Education from its 'modern' encyclopaedic scope?
options: The modern view expands beyond mere physical training to embrace health education, recreation, dance, and aquatics as integrated components
The modern view restricts Physical Education strictly to competitive interschool sports
The narrow view includes intramural and extramural programmes while the modern view excludes them
There is no meaningful distinction; both views are identical in practice
questions.explanation: The modern, encyclopaedic conception of Physical Education broadens the traditional 'physical training' focus to integrate health education, recreation, dance, gymnastics, and aquatics as interconnected components of total human development.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In Ancient Greece, the Olympic Games and associated gymnastic training were primarily organised to
options: provide purely recreational entertainment devoid of religious or civic meaning
honour the gods, prepare citizens physically and militarily, and celebrate ideals of balanced body and mind (kalokagathia)
train soldiers exclusively for professional standing armies
satisfy trade guild requirements for craftsmen
questions.explanation: Ancient Greek physical culture combined religious festival, civic pride, military preparedness, and the philosophical ideal of a harmonious, balanced development of body and mind.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Physical training in Ancient Rome differed markedly from the Greek approach chiefly because Roman practice
options: emphasised aesthetic and intellectual balance over utilitarian ends
banned all forms of public physical contests
was almost entirely utilitarian, geared toward military conditioning and gladiatorial spectacle rather than holistic education
focused solely on women's participation in athletics
questions.explanation: Whereas the Greeks pursued a philosophical ideal of balanced body-and-mind development, Roman physical activity was largely utilitarian, oriented toward military fitness and public gladiatorial entertainment.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Clark Hetherington's 'New Physical Education' philosophy is best remembered for classifying the objectives of Physical Education into which four domains?
options: Organic, psychomotor, cognitive, and aesthetic objectives only
Physical fitness, offensive skill, defensive skill, and endurance objectives only
Military, religious, vocational, and recreational objectives
Organic (physical), psychomotor (neuromuscular), character (civic-moral), and intellectual (mental) objectives
questions.explanation: Hetherington's influential framework identified organic, psychomotor, character, and intellectual development as the four fundamental objectives that Physical Education should serve.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Dudley Allen Sargent's most notable contribution to the field of Physical Education was his pioneering work in
options: anthropometric measurement and the individualised prescription of exercise based on a person's physical assessment
banning competitive sport from school curricula
establishing the modern Olympic Games
codifying the rules of association football
questions.explanation: Sargent developed systematic anthropometric measurement techniques and advocated prescribing exercise programmes tailored to an individual's specific physical assessment and needs.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Thomas Wood's philosophy, encapsulated in the phrase 'education through the physical' rather than 'education of the physical', emphasised that
options: physical activity has no bearing on cognitive or social learning
physical activity should serve as a medium for total personality development, not merely a means of training the body in isolation
only elite athletes benefit from Physical Education
Physical Education should be entirely separate from the general school curriculum
questions.explanation: Wood argued that physical activity should be used as an educational medium to develop the whole person -- socially, mentally, and morally -- rather than treating the body as an isolated object of training.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: John Dewey's progressive education philosophy influenced Physical Education mainly by promoting the idea that
options: learning occurs best through rote memorisation of rules and regulations
children should be excluded from decision-making in physical activities
children learn most effectively through direct experience and purposeful activity, supporting play and movement as valid vehicles for learning
Physical Education should be reserved only for military academies
questions.explanation: Dewey's experiential, 'learning by doing' philosophy reinforced the value of play and physical activity as legitimate, purposeful avenues for a child's total educational development.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best exemplifies the 'character/social' objective of Physical Education, as distinct from the organic or psychomotor objectives?
options: Improved cardiovascular endurance from repeated interval training
Increased muscular strength from resistance training
Refined balance and coordination during a gymnastic routine
Development of cooperation, sportsmanship, leadership, and fair play through team games
questions.explanation: The character/social objective concerns traits such as cooperation, discipline, leadership, and sportsmanship cultivated through participation, distinct from purely physiological (organic) or skill-based (psychomotor) gains.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Naturalism, as a philosophical orientation applied to Physical Education, primarily advocates that
options: activities and play should follow the natural interests, instincts, and developmental readiness of the learner rather than adult-imposed formalism
physical activities should be rigidly standardised regardless of a child's developmental stage or interest
only indoor, apparatus-based gymnastics should be taught
competition should be entirely abolished from all programmes
questions.explanation: Naturalism emphasises designing physical activity around the learner's natural instincts, interests, and stage of development rather than imposing rigid, formal adult structures.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The modern Olympic Games, revived in 1896, are most directly credited to the efforts of
options: Clark Hetherington
Baron Pierre de Coubertin
Thomas Wood
Dudley Sargent
questions.explanation: Baron Pierre de Coubertin is credited with reviving the ancient Olympic tradition, founding the International Olympic Committee and organising the first modern Games in Athens in 1896.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In pre-colonial Nigerian society, traditional wrestling, canoe regattas, and hunting expeditions served Physical Education-related purposes chiefly by
options: providing purely religious ritual with no bearing on physical skill
being restricted exclusively to royalty for private entertainment
developing physical fitness, courage, and social cohesion while marking rites of passage within the community
replacing formal education entirely in traditional society
questions.explanation: Traditional Nigerian physical activities such as wrestling and regattas built fitness, courage, and communal identity, and often functioned as rites of passage integrated into the community's social fabric.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which statement most accurately distinguishes the 'aims' from the 'objectives' of Physical Education?
options: Aims and objectives are entirely synonymous with no distinction in scope
Objectives apply only to elite athletes while aims apply only to beginners
Aims concern only mental development while objectives concern only physical development
Aims are broad, long-term statements of overall purpose, while objectives are specific, measurable outcomes derived from those aims
questions.explanation: Aims represent broad, overarching statements of purpose for a programme, whereas objectives are the specific, measurable, and attainable outcomes designed to fulfil those broader aims.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A key rationale for including dance and aquatics within the broadened scope of modern Physical Education curricula is that they
options: extend the range of movement experiences, fitness benefits, and safety skills beyond traditional competitive team sports
have no measurable physical or health benefits and are included purely for entertainment
are only appropriate for professional athletes
were historically excluded from all ancient civilisations' physical culture
questions.explanation: Dance and aquatics broaden movement experience, contribute to fitness, coordination, and rhythm, and in the case of swimming, impart essential water-safety skills, complementing traditional competitive sports.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the psychomotor objective of Physical Education?
options: The cultivation of moral values such as honesty and fair play
The development of neuromuscular skills such as coordination, balance, agility, and efficient movement patterns
The strengthening of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems alone
The acquisition of theoretical knowledge about sports history
questions.explanation: The psychomotor objective specifically targets neuromuscular skill development -- coordination, balance, agility, and efficient, purposeful movement patterns.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The axial skeleton, one of the two major divisions of the human skeletal system, is composed of the
options: upper and lower limbs together with the pectoral and pelvic girdles
carpals, tarsals, and phalanges only
skull, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum
clavicle and scapula only
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton comprises the skull, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum, forming the central axis of the body, while the appendicular skeleton comprises the limbs and girdles.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Synovial fluid, found within the cavity of freely movable (synovial) joints, primarily functions to
options: transport oxygen directly to muscle fibres
stimulate bone growth at the epiphyseal plate
regulate the joint's blood pressure
lubricate the joint, reduce friction between articulating bone surfaces, and supply nutrients to the articular cartilage
questions.explanation: Synovial fluid lubricates synovial joints, minimises friction between the articulating bone surfaces, and helps nourish the avascular articular cartilage.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae at the top of the spinal column, which permits the rotational 'no' head movement, is best classified as a
options: pivot joint
hinge joint
ball-and-socket joint
saddle joint
questions.explanation: The atlanto-axial joint is a pivot joint, allowing rotational movement of the head, such as shaking the head to indicate 'no'.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The carpometacarpal joint at the base of the thumb, which allows the thumb to oppose the fingers, is classified anatomically as a
options: hinge joint
saddle joint
pivot joint
gliding (plane) joint
questions.explanation: The joint at the base of the thumb is a saddle joint, a shape permitting the wide range of motion, including opposition, characteristic of the human thumb.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: During elbow flexion performed by the biceps brachii, the triceps brachii acts as the
options: synergist, assisting the biceps in producing the same movement
fixator, stabilising the shoulder joint only
antagonist, relaxing while the biceps (the agonist) contracts to produce the movement
prime mover, generating the primary force for flexion
questions.explanation: In antagonistic muscle pairs, the triceps brachii (antagonist) relaxes and lengthens while the biceps brachii (agonist/prime mover) contracts to produce elbow flexion.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: An isometric muscle contraction is best described as one in which the muscle
options: shortens while generating tension, producing visible joint movement
lengthens under tension while controlling a movement, such as lowering a weight
is completely relaxed with no tension developed
generates tension and develops force without any appreciable change in its length or visible joint movement
questions.explanation: An isometric contraction generates muscular tension without a change in muscle length or visible movement at the joint, as when pushing against an immovable object.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: When a weightlifter slowly lowers a barbell under control, the primary muscles acting are undergoing which type of contraction?
options: Eccentric contraction, as the muscle lengthens while still generating tension
Concentric contraction, as the muscle shortens
Isometric contraction, as the muscle length remains constant
Isokinetic contraction at a fixed, machine-controlled speed only
questions.explanation: Lowering a weight under control involves an eccentric contraction, in which the muscle lengthens while still producing tension to control the movement.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Blood pressure readings are expressed as two values, for example 120/80 mmHg. The lower value (80) represents the
options: systolic pressure, generated when the ventricles contract
diastolic pressure, the pressure in the arteries when the heart relaxes between beats
pulse rate in beats per minute
stroke volume of the left ventricle
questions.explanation: The lower reading is the diastolic pressure, representing arterial pressure while the heart muscle relaxes between contractions; the higher reading (systolic) reflects pressure during ventricular contraction.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Cardiac output is best defined as
options: the resting heart rate measured over one minute
the maximum oxygen uptake achievable during exercise
the total volume of blood ejected by the left ventricle in one minute, calculated as heart rate multiplied by stroke volume
the total blood volume contained within the entire circulatory system
questions.explanation: Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume, representing the total volume of blood the heart pumps out per minute.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A well-conditioned athlete typically exhibits a lower resting heart rate than an untrained individual mainly because regular aerobic training leads to
options: a smaller, weaker heart with reduced stroke volume
complete cessation of the need for cardiac contraction
a permanent increase in resting blood pressure
cardiac hypertrophy and increased stroke volume, allowing the same cardiac output to be achieved with fewer beats per minute
questions.explanation: Training-induced cardiac hypertrophy increases stroke volume (the volume of blood ejected per beat), so the heart can maintain adequate cardiac output at a lower resting heart rate.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Tidal volume, a key measure in respiratory physiology, refers to
options: the volume of air inhaled or exhaled in a single normal, resting breath
the maximum volume of air that can be forcibly exhaled after a maximum inhalation
the total lung capacity including residual volume
the volume of air remaining in the lungs after maximal expiration
questions.explanation: Tidal volume is the amount of air moved into or out of the lungs during a single normal breath at rest, distinct from vital capacity or residual volume.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Gas exchange between inhaled air and the bloodstream occurs primarily at the
options: bronchioles, via active transport mechanisms
alveoli, through diffusion across their thin, richly capillarised walls
trachea, through mucus-lined ciliated cells
diaphragm, through direct muscular contraction
questions.explanation: The alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries; their thin walls and large surface area allow oxygen and carbon dioxide to diffuse efficiently between the air and the blood.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and flattens, which primarily causes
options: a decrease in thoracic cavity volume and a rise in internal air pressure, forcing air out of the lungs
complete cessation of airflow into or out of the lungs
an increase in thoracic cavity volume, lowering internal air pressure below atmospheric pressure so that air flows into the lungs
direct contraction of the alveoli to actively pull in air
questions.explanation: Diaphragmatic contraction enlarges the thoracic cavity, reducing internal pressure below atmospheric pressure, which draws air into the lungs (Boyle's Law in action).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: 'Oxygen debt' following intense anaerobic exercise refers to
options: a permanent reduction in an individual's maximum lung capacity
the total oxygen consumed throughout an entire exercise session
a medical condition requiring hospitalisation
the volume of oxygen required after exercise to restore the body to its resting physiological state and clear accumulated lactic acid
questions.explanation: Oxygen debt describes the extra oxygen consumed during recovery to restore ATP and phosphocreatine stores and metabolise accumulated lactic acid built up during intense anaerobic effort.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which scenario best illustrates the practical distinction between aerobic and anaerobic exercise?
options: A marathon runner sustaining a steady moderate pace for two hours relies mainly on aerobic metabolism, whereas a 100m sprinter relies predominantly on anaerobic metabolism
Both marathon running and 100m sprinting rely exclusively on anaerobic metabolism
A marathon runner relies on anaerobic metabolism while a sprinter relies on aerobic metabolism
Aerobic and anaerobic metabolism are interchangeable terms with no physiological difference
questions.explanation: Prolonged, moderate-intensity activities like marathon running are sustained by aerobic (oxygen-dependent) metabolism, while brief, maximal-intensity efforts like sprinting rely predominantly on anaerobic energy pathways.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The reflex arc, a fundamental unit of nervous system function relevant to rapid movement responses in sport, typically follows which sequence?
options: Effector, motor neuron, spinal cord, sensory neuron, receptor
Receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord (relay), motor neuron, effector
Motor neuron, receptor, effector, sensory neuron
Effector, receptor, spinal cord, sensory neuron
questions.explanation: A reflex arc begins at a receptor, travels via a sensory neuron to the spinal cord (often through a relay neuron), then out via a motor neuron to an effector (muscle), producing a rapid, involuntary response.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: An athlete with a somatotype classified as ectomorphic would typically be characterised by which physical profile, making them well suited to endurance events such as long-distance running?
options: A short, stocky, heavily muscled frame with a low centre of gravity
A rounded frame with a high proportion of body fat and a soft physique
A linear, slender frame with narrow shoulders, low body fat, and limited muscle bulk
A broad, muscular frame excelling primarily in power and strength events
questions.explanation: Ectomorphs are characterised by a lean, slender, linear build with minimal fat and muscle mass, a physique often advantageous for endurance-based activities.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A mesomorphic somatotype, often associated with success in power and sprint events, is characterised primarily by
options: a slender frame with minimal muscle development
a soft, rounded physique with a high proportion of stored body fat
an absence of any distinguishable muscular development
a well-developed, muscular physique with broad shoulders, a narrow waist, and low body fat
questions.explanation: Mesomorphs possess a naturally muscular, athletic build with broad shoulders and low body fat, often conferring advantages in strength- and power-based sports.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: An endomorphic somatotype is primarily characterised by
options: a rounded body shape with a relatively high proportion of body fat and a soft musculature
a lean, fragile frame with very low body fat
extreme muscularity with minimal fat storage
unusually long limbs relative to torso length
questions.explanation: Endomorphs typically present a rounder body shape with higher body fat storage and a softer muscular definition compared to mesomorphs or ectomorphs.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Scoliosis, a postural defect of the spine, is best defined as
options: an exaggerated outward (posterior) curvature of the thoracic spine, producing a hunchback appearance
an abnormal lateral (sideways) curvature of the vertebral column
an exaggerated inward (anterior) curvature of the lumbar spine
a flattening of the medial longitudinal arch of the foot
questions.explanation: Scoliosis is characterised by an abnormal sideways curvature of the spine, distinguishing it from kyphosis (excessive outward thoracic curve) and lordosis (excessive inward lumbar curve).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Kyphosis, a postural defect distinct from scoliosis and lordosis, refers specifically to
options: a lateral curvature of the spine visible from behind
an excessive inward curvature of the lumbar spine, causing the abdomen to protrude
an excessive outward (posterior) curvature of the thoracic region of the spine, producing a rounded, hunchback appearance
a lateral deviation of the big toe
questions.explanation: Kyphosis is an exaggerated outward curvature of the thoracic spine, resulting in a rounded or hunched upper back, distinct from the lateral curve of scoliosis or the inward curve of lordosis.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Lordosis, a postural defect affecting the lower back, is best described as
options: an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine
an exaggerated outward curvature of the upper (thoracic) spine
a collapse of the transverse arch of the foot
an exaggerated inward (anterior) curvature of the lumbar spine, often causing the abdomen and buttocks to protrude
questions.explanation: Lordosis involves an excessive inward curve of the lumbar (lower back) region, often causing the abdomen and buttocks to protrude forward and backward respectively.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Flatfoot (pes planus), a common postural/structural defect, is characterised by
options: the collapse or absence of the medial longitudinal arch, causing the entire sole to make contact with the ground
an abnormally high medial longitudinal arch of the foot
a lateral curvature of the vertebral column
an inward rotation of the knee joints (knock-knees)
