questions.explanation: Flatfoot involves the flattening or collapse of the medial longitudinal arch, so that most or all of the sole of the foot contacts the ground while standing.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which corrective approach is most appropriate for a mild, non-structural (postural) case of kyphosis identified in a school-age child?
options: Immediate spinal surgery in all cases
Targeted postural and strengthening exercises for the back extensor muscles, combined with attention to correct sitting and standing posture
Complete avoidance of all physical activity
Prescription of anabolic steroids to build back muscle rapidly
questions.explanation: Mild postural kyphosis is typically managed through targeted corrective exercises strengthening the back extensors and improving postural habits, reserving surgery for severe structural cases.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In biomechanics, the principle of stability states that an object (such as a rugby player in a defensive stance) becomes more stable when it has
options: a high centre of gravity and a narrow base of support
a centre of gravity located entirely outside the base of support
a low centre of gravity and a wide base of support, with the line of gravity falling within the base
no base of support at all
questions.explanation: Stability is enhanced by lowering the centre of gravity, widening the base of support, and keeping the line of gravity within that base -- principles athletes exploit in stances such as a wrestler's crouch.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Newton's Third Law of Motion, stating that every action produces an equal and opposite reaction, is best illustrated in sport by which example?
options: A ball continuing in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force
A heavier shot put requiring more force to achieve the same acceleration as a lighter one
An athlete's body remaining at rest until a force is applied
A sprinter pushing backward against the starting blocks, propelling their body forward
questions.explanation: Newton's Third Law is demonstrated when a sprinter's foot pushes backward against the blocks (action), and the blocks push the sprinter's body forward with equal and opposite force (reaction).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: During the sprint start in track athletics, an athlete's initial acceleration off the blocks is most improved by
options: maintaining a low, forward-leaning body position and driving powerfully with both legs through full extension
standing fully upright immediately upon the gun to maximise stride length
looking upward and backward to check competitors' positions
starting with the front foot fully extended and the rear foot flat
questions.explanation: Optimal sprint starts require a low, forward-leaning drive phase with powerful, complete leg extension from the blocks to maximise horizontal acceleration before gradually rising to an upright running posture.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In middle-distance track events such as the 800m and 1500m, tactical pacing is critical mainly because athletes must
options: sprint at maximum speed for the entire race distance without variation
balance aerobic and anaerobic energy contributions, conserving energy for a decisive finishing kick while maintaining competitive positioning
avoid overtaking any competitor at any point in the race
complete the race using only anaerobic energy pathways
questions.explanation: Middle-distance running demands a blend of aerobic endurance and anaerobic capacity; successful athletes pace themselves to conserve energy for a strong finishing kick while staying tactically well positioned.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The steeplechase, a distinctive long/middle-distance track event, is primarily characterised by
options: athletes running on an indoor track exclusively with no obstacles
a race run entirely underwater
competitors negotiating fixed barriers and a water jump interspersed along the race distance
a relay format involving four runners passing a baton
questions.explanation: The steeplechase requires athletes to clear fixed barriers and a water jump at intervals around the track, distinguishing it from standard flat middle/long-distance races.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In a 4x400m relay, unlike the 4x100m relay, incoming and outgoing runners typically perform which type of baton exchange, given the greater fatigue and spacing involved?
options: A blind exchange, where the receiving runner does not look back at the baton
No exchange is required in the 4x400m relay
An exchange performed entirely outside the marked takeover zone
A visual exchange, where the receiving runner looks back to watch the baton into their hand
questions.explanation: Because runners in the 4x400m relay are typically more fatigued and speeds are lower than in the 4x100m, a visual exchange -- where the receiver watches the baton into their hand -- is commonly used for greater reliability.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: According to World Athletics rules, the baton exchange in relay races must be completed entirely within
options: a designated 20-metre takeover zone marked on the track
the first 10 metres of the entire track
any point along the entire back straight
a zone determined solely by the head coach before the race
questions.explanation: Relay baton exchanges must occur within a marked 20-metre takeover zone; a baton passed outside this zone results in disqualification.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In the long jump, a competitor's attempt is ruled a 'foul' (no jump) chiefly when the athlete
options: lands beyond the marked sand pit boundary only
oversteps the takeoff board, with any part of the foot extending beyond its front edge into the plasticine indicator before jumping
takes fewer than three steps in the approach run
jumps using a foot other than their preferred takeoff foot
questions.explanation: A long jump attempt is declared a foul if the athlete's foot breaks the vertical plane of the takeoff board's front edge, as registered on the adjoining indicator board, regardless of how far the jump itself measures.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The 'Fosbury Flop' technique revolutionised which field event by having athletes clear the bar backwards, landing on their upper back and shoulders?
options: The long jump
The triple jump
The high jump
The pole vault
questions.explanation: The Fosbury Flop, popularised by Dick Fosbury, is a high jump technique in which the athlete clears the bar head-first and backwards, landing on the upper back, and remains the dominant technique in elite high jump today.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The triple jump is officially defined by a specific sequence of movements. Which sequence correctly describes it?
options: Three consecutive jumps performed off alternating feet with no fixed order
A jump, followed by a hop, followed by a step, in any order chosen by the athlete
A single jump performed three times in succession by three different athletes
A hop, followed by a step, followed by a jump, with the hop landing on the same foot used for takeoff
questions.explanation: The triple jump comprises a hop (landing on the same foot that took off), a step (landing on the opposite foot), and a final jump into the pit -- performed in that fixed sequence.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In the shot put, which rule governs how the implement must be legally released to ensure a valid attempt?
options: The shot must be 'put' -- pushed from the shoulder with one hand, without dropping behind the shoulder line during the delivery
The shot must be thrown using a full arm swing from behind the body, similar to a discus throw
The shot may be thrown using either hand or both hands simultaneously from any position
The shot must be released after a full 360-degree spin identical to the discus technique
questions.explanation: Shot put rules require the shot to be 'put' (pushed) from the shoulder using one hand, without the athlete allowing the implement to drop behind the line of the shoulders during the delivery action.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In the javelin throw, a valid, measurable attempt specifically requires that the javelin
options: lands anywhere within the throwing sector, regardless of orientation
lands within the marked sector with its metal tip striking the ground first, ahead of any other part of the implement
is thrown using a full circular spinning technique similar to the discus
be released while standing entirely outside the runway
questions.explanation: A javelin throw is only counted as valid if the metal tip strikes the ground first within the marked sector; the flat landing of the shaft on the ground invalidates the attempt.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The decathlon, a multi-event athletics competition for men, consists of how many events contested over two days?
options: Seven events
Twelve events
Ten events
Five events
questions.explanation: The decathlon comprises ten track and field events contested over two consecutive days, testing an athlete's versatility across sprints, jumps, throws, and endurance running.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In a standard football (soccer) match, which of the following situations does NOT constitute an offside offence, despite the attacker being in an offside position?
options: The attacker receives the ball directly from a teammate's through pass while ahead of the second-last defender
The attacker actively interferes with an opponent's ability to play the ball while offside
The attacker gains an advantage by playing a ball that rebounded off the goalpost while offside
The attacker receives the ball directly from a corner kick, throw-in, or goal kick
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of the Game, a player cannot be penalised for offside if they receive the ball directly from a corner kick, throw-in, or goal kick, even if positioned beyond the second-last defender.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In football, the key distinction between a direct free kick and an indirect free kick is that
options: a goal may be scored straight from a direct free kick without the ball touching another player, whereas a goal from an indirect free kick requires the ball to touch another player first
an indirect free kick can score directly while a direct free kick cannot
both types of free kicks are identical in every respect
a direct free kick may only be taken by the goalkeeper
questions.explanation: A direct free kick allows a goal to be scored directly against the opposing team, while a goal from an indirect free kick can only count if the ball touches another player (of either team) before entering the goal.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Under current standard FIFA competition rules, the maximum number of substitutions permitted per team during normal time in most top-level matches is
options: three substitutions
five substitutions
unlimited substitutions with no cap
two substitutions
questions.explanation: Following amendments widely adopted after 2020, most top-level competitions permit up to five substitutions per team during the normal 90 minutes of play, typically within a limited number of stoppages.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In basketball, the shot clock -- a rule requiring a team to attempt a shot within a set time after gaining possession -- is generally set, under FIBA rules, at
options: 10 seconds
45 seconds
24 seconds
8 seconds
questions.explanation: Under FIBA and most professional basketball rules, a team must attempt a shot that at least hits the rim within 24 seconds of gaining possession, or a shot-clock violation is called.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In basketball, the '8-second rule' specifically requires that a team
options: complete a shot attempt within 8 seconds of gaining possession
hold the ball for at least 8 seconds before attempting a shot
substitute a player at least once every 8 seconds
advance the ball from its backcourt into the frontcourt within 8 seconds of gaining possession
questions.explanation: The 8-second rule requires a team to move the ball from its own backcourt across the half-court line into the frontcourt within 8 seconds of gaining possession, or a violation is called.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In basketball, which of the following best distinguishes a 'technical foul' from an ordinary 'personal foul'?
options: A technical foul involves unsportsmanlike conduct, dissent, or a rule violation unrelated to normal physical contact during play, whereas a personal foul involves illegal physical contact against an opponent
A personal foul is always more severe and results in ejection, while a technical foul carries no penalty
There is no distinction; both terms describe identical infractions
A technical foul can only be committed by a coach, never by a player
questions.explanation: A personal foul arises from illegal physical contact with an opponent during play, while a technical foul penalises unsportsmanlike conduct, dissent toward officials, or procedural violations not involving normal player contact.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In volleyball, the specialised defensive player known as the 'libero' is subject to which distinctive rule?
options: The libero may serve, block, and attack the ball from anywhere on the court like any other player
The libero wears a different-coloured uniform, cannot block or attack the ball above net height from the front zone, and has restricted service rights depending on the rule set in use
The libero must always be the team captain
The libero is prohibited from ever touching the ball during a match
questions.explanation: The libero is a designated defensive specialist who wears a contrasting uniform and is restricted from blocking or completing an attack hit above the top of the net from the front zone, with limited serving permitted under current rules.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A standard volleyball set (excluding a potential deciding fifth set) is won by the first team to reach
options: 21 points, requiring a two-point advantage
15 points with no minimum winning margin required
25 points, requiring at least a two-point advantage over the opponent
30 points with sudden-death scoring at 29-29
questions.explanation: Standard volleyball sets are played to 25 points (15 points in a deciding fifth set), with the set won only if the leading team has at least a two-point advantage.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In badminton, a standard match is generally contested as
options: the best of five 15-point games
a single game played to 30 points
the best of three games, each played to 11 points
the best of three games, each played to 21 points with a two-point winning margin required (subject to a cap)
questions.explanation: Standard badminton matches are played as the best of three games, with each game won by the first side to reach 21 points, requiring at least a two-point lead (up to a maximum cap of 30 points).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A key equipment distinction in badminton is that the shuttlecock, unlike a ball used in tennis or table tennis, is characterised by
options: a conical shape with a rounded cork or synthetic base and a skirt of feathers (or synthetic material) that causes rapid aerodynamic deceleration
a solid rubber sphere with no feathers or synthetic skirt
a perfectly spherical shape identical to a tennis ball but smaller
a hollow celluloid or plastic sphere used exclusively outdoors
questions.explanation: The shuttlecock's conical feathered (or synthetic) skirt attached to a rounded base creates high aerodynamic drag, causing it to decelerate rapidly in flight -- a distinctive feature not shared by balls used in tennis or table tennis.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In team handball, a field player who receives the ball is permitted to hold it and take a maximum of how many steps before passing, dribbling, or shooting?
options: Five steps
Three steps
Two steps
No limit on steps as long as the ball is not dribbled
questions.explanation: In handball, a player may take a maximum of three steps while holding the ball before they must pass, shoot, dribble, or release it, or a 'steps' violation is called.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In field hockey, players are permitted to play the ball legally using only which part of the stick?
options: Either the flat face or the rounded back edge of the stick, interchangeably
Only the rounded back edge of the stick
Only the flat (non-rounded) face of the stick
Any part of the stick, including the handle
questions.explanation: Field hockey rules restrict legal play to the flat face of the stick; deliberately playing the ball with the rounded back edge results in a foul.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In cricket, a batsman is given out 'leg before wicket' (LBW) essentially when
options: the batsman's leg touches the boundary rope while running
the batsman is struck by the ball anywhere on the body while standing outside the crease
the fielding team appeals after the batsman completes a run
the ball strikes the batsman's leg pad and, in the umpire's judgement, would otherwise have gone on to hit the stumps, subject to specified conditions
questions.explanation: An LBW dismissal occurs when the ball strikes part of the batsman's body (typically the leg) in line with the stumps, and the umpire judges that the ball would have gone on to hit the stumps, subject to specific conditions in the Laws of Cricket.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In tennis, when a set reaches a score of 6-6 games, play is typically decided by which mechanism under standard modern rules?
options: A tiebreak game, generally won by the first player to reach 7 points with at least a two-point lead
The set continues indefinitely until one player leads by two clear games with no tiebreak
The match is immediately declared a draw
The set is awarded to whichever player won the most total points
questions.explanation: Under standard modern rules, a set reaching 6-6 in games is typically decided by a tiebreak game, won by the first player to reach 7 points with a minimum two-point advantage.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes the role of a 'referee' from that of a 'linesman/assistant referee' in football officiating?
options: The linesman has final authority over all decisions, overriding the referee
The referee has overall authority to make final decisions on the pitch, while the assistant referee/linesman primarily signals offside, throw-ins, and out-of-play situations to assist the referee
Both officials have completely identical powers and duties
Only the linesman may award penalty kicks
questions.explanation: The referee holds ultimate authority to make and enforce decisions during a match, while assistant referees (linesmen) support by signalling matters such as offside, ball out of play, and throw-ins/corners.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A standard FIFA-regulation football pitch for international adult matches must have a length and width falling within which approximate range?
options: Length 30-50 metres; width 20-30 metres
Length 200-250 metres; width 100-150 metres
Length 90-120 metres; width 45-90 metres
Fixed dimensions of exactly 50 by 30 metres with no permitted variation
questions.explanation: FIFA regulations specify a football pitch length of 90-120 metres and a width of 45-90 metres for international matches, with stricter ranges applying to international fixtures specifically.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A basketball hoop (rim) is regulated to be mounted at a standard height above the playing floor of
options: 2.44 metres (8 feet)
3.66 metres (12 feet)
2.13 metres (7 feet)
3.05 metres (10 feet)
questions.explanation: The basketball rim is standardised at a height of 3.05 metres (10 feet) above the playing surface in virtually all levels of organised competition.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: In gymnastics, a forward roll is technically distinguished from a backward roll mainly by the
options: direction of body rotation relative to the direction of travel, and the corresponding hand/head placement used to protect the neck during rotation
use of apparatus only in the forward roll and none in the backward roll
requirement that only the backward roll be performed on a balance beam
complete absence of any tucking of the body in a forward roll
questions.explanation: A forward roll rotates the body forward over a tucked head with hands placed ahead to guide the rotation, while a backward roll rotates backward, requiring the hands to be placed beside the head to push off and protect the neck.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The balance beam, an apparatus used in women's artistic gymnastics, is officially set at a standard height and width of approximately
options: 500 cm high and 100 cm wide
125 cm high and 10 cm wide
10 cm high and 125 cm wide
No standard dimensions are specified for this apparatus
questions.explanation: The competition balance beam is approximately 125 cm above the floor and only about 10 cm wide, demanding exceptional balance, precision, and core control from gymnasts.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The front crawl (freestyle) swimming stroke is technically distinguished from breaststroke chiefly by its
options: simultaneous, symmetrical arm pull with a whip-like frog kick performed underwater throughout
complete absence of any leg kick
alternating overarm arm recovery combined with a continuous flutter kick, generally the fastest recognised competitive stroke
requirement that swimmers remain submerged for the entire length of the pool
questions.explanation: Front crawl (freestyle) uses an alternating overarm recovery with a continuous flutter kick and is the fastest of the competitive strokes, unlike breaststroke's simultaneous symmetrical arm pull and frog kick.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The butterfly stroke in competitive swimming is characterised by which distinctive combination of movements?
options: An alternating overarm recovery paired with a flutter kick
Swimming on the back with an alternating arm and leg action
A frog-like breaststroke kick combined with an alternating arm stroke
A simultaneous, symmetrical over-water arm recovery combined with a simultaneous 'dolphin' kick of both legs together
questions.explanation: Butterfly requires both arms to recover simultaneously over the water while both legs perform a synchronised undulating dolphin kick, making it one of the most physically demanding competitive strokes.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: When attempting a water rescue of a struggling swimmer without entering the water, the recommended first-aid priority for a bystander is to
options: attempt a reach, throw, or wade-assisted rescue using an object such as a pole, rope, or flotation device before considering direct contact
dive in immediately regardless of personal swimming ability or training
wait for the swimmer to reach the poolside unaided in every circumstance
shout instructions only, with no attempt to provide any physical aid
questions.explanation: Water safety protocol prioritises 'reach or throw, don't go' -- using poles, ropes, or flotation devices to assist a struggling swimmer from land before a trained rescuer considers entering the water directly.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Rhythmic gymnastics is distinguished from artistic gymnastics primarily by its incorporation of
options: apparatus such as the vaulting horse and parallel bars
handheld apparatus such as ribbon, hoop, ball, and clubs performed to music, without tumbling on hard apparatus
exclusively male competitors performing on the pommel horse
swimming-based movement sequences
questions.explanation: Rhythmic gymnastics combines dance-like movement with handheld apparatus (ribbon, hoop, ball, clubs, rope) performed to music, distinguishing it from the apparatus-based tumbling of artistic gymnastics.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A well-balanced diet suitable for an endurance athlete in the days before a major competition typically emphasises which nutritional strategy, commonly known as carbohydrate loading?
options: Drastically reducing all food intake to lower body weight before competition
Eliminating carbohydrates entirely in favour of pure protein intake
Progressively increasing carbohydrate intake in the days before competition to maximise glycogen stores in the muscles and liver
Consuming only fats in the 48 hours preceding competition
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate loading involves strategically increasing carbohydrate consumption in the days before an endurance event to maximise glycogen stores, delaying fatigue during prolonged exercise.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A 'complete protein' source, important for athletes' muscle repair and growth, is best defined as one that
options: contains only carbohydrates with no amino acids present
lacks several essential amino acids, as typically found in most animal products
is defined solely by its total caloric content rather than amino acid composition
contains all nine essential amino acids in adequate proportions, such as those found in eggs, meat, fish, and dairy
questions.explanation: Complete proteins supply all nine essential amino acids in adequate amounts; common sources include eggs, meat, fish, and dairy, whereas many single plant sources are 'incomplete' proteins.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Scurvy, a deficiency disease affecting connective tissue and gum health, results specifically from a prolonged deficiency of
options: Vitamin C
Vitamin D
Vitamin B1 (thiamine)
Calcium
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from a prolonged deficiency of Vitamin C, which is essential for collagen synthesis; symptoms include bleeding gums, joint pain, and poor wound healing.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Rickets, a bone deformity disease common in children, arises primarily from a deficiency of
options: Vitamin C alone
Vitamin D and calcium, impairing proper bone mineralisation
Protein alone, with no involvement of minerals or vitamins
Vitamin B12 exclusively
questions.explanation: Rickets results from inadequate Vitamin D and calcium, impairing bone mineralisation in growing children and leading to soft, weakened, and deformed bones.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Iron-deficiency anaemia, a condition that can significantly reduce an athlete's aerobic performance, occurs because insufficient iron impairs the body's ability to
options: absorb dietary fats efficiently
produce sufficient white blood cells to fight infection
synthesise adequate haemoglobin, reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity
regulate blood clotting after injury
questions.explanation: Iron is essential for haemoglobin synthesis; a deficiency reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of red blood cells, causing fatigue and diminished aerobic exercise performance.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Anabolic steroids, a class of substances banned under most sporting anti-doping codes, are prohibited mainly because they
options: have no measurable physiological effect on the athlete's body
are only used to treat minor colds and coughs
are legal nutritional supplements freely available to all competitors
artificially enhance muscle mass and strength beyond what natural training achieves, providing an unfair competitive advantage while posing serious health risks
questions.explanation: Anabolic steroids mimic testosterone to artificially boost muscle mass and strength, conferring an unfair advantage while carrying serious risks such as cardiovascular disease, liver damage, and hormonal disruption.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Stimulant doping agents such as amphetamines are banned in competitive sport primarily because they
options: artificially mask fatigue, increase alertness and heart rate, and can enable athletes to push beyond safe physiological limits, risking cardiovascular harm
have no impact on alertness, heart rate, or fatigue perception
are required as a routine part of daily athletic nutrition
only affect an athlete's sense of taste
questions.explanation: Stimulants like amphetamines mask fatigue and heighten alertness and heart rate, allowing athletes to exceed safe physiological limits, which creates an unfair advantage and significant cardiovascular risk.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Chronic alcohol abuse impairs athletic performance and safety most directly by
options: improving reaction time and fine motor coordination
impairing coordination, reaction time, and judgement, while also disrupting sleep and long-term liver and cardiovascular health
enhancing endurance capacity during prolonged exercise
having no measurable effect on the nervous system
questions.explanation: Alcohol depresses central nervous system function, impairing coordination, reaction time, and judgement, disrupts restorative sleep, and causes long-term damage to the liver and cardiovascular system.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Chronic tobacco/cigarette smoking is particularly associated with a significantly increased risk of which condition, given its direct impact on the respiratory system?
options: Improved lung capacity and enhanced aerobic performance
Complete immunity to all respiratory infections
Chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and lung cancer due to damage of the airways and alveoli
Enhanced haemoglobin oxygen-carrying capacity
questions.explanation: Tobacco smoke damages the airway lining and alveoli over time, substantially increasing the risk of chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and lung cancer, and impairing overall respiratory efficiency.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: An open (compound) fracture is distinguished from a closed (simple) fracture chiefly by the fact that in an open fracture
options: the bone is merely bruised with no actual break occurring
the bone bends and partially cracks without fully breaking, as seen typically in children
there is no pain or swelling present at all
the broken bone penetrates through the skin, creating an open wound with a risk of infection
questions.explanation: An open (compound) fracture involves the broken bone piercing through the skin, creating an open wound and a significant risk of infection, unlike a closed fracture where the skin remains intact.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A greenstick fracture, a type of bone injury seen predominantly in children, is best described as one in which the bone
options: bends and cracks incompletely on one side without breaking all the way through, due to the relative flexibility of a child's bone
breaks completely into two separate fragments
shatters into multiple small fragments at the point of impact
dislocates entirely from its adjoining joint
questions.explanation: A greenstick fracture occurs when a still-pliable, immature bone bends and cracks on one side without breaking completely through, a pattern seen mainly in children due to their more flexible bone structure.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following most accurately distinguishes a sprain from a strain as sports injuries?
options: A sprain and a strain refer to the exact same type of tissue damage
A sprain involves damage to a ligament connecting bone to bone at a joint, while a strain involves damage to a muscle or its tendon
A sprain always involves a complete bone fracture, while a strain never does
A strain refers only to injuries of the skin, while a sprain refers only to injuries of bone
questions.explanation: A sprain is an injury to a ligament (connecting bone to bone) typically at a joint, whereas a strain involves overstretching or tearing of a muscle or its tendon (connecting muscle to bone).

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: A joint dislocation is best distinguished from a sprain by the fact that a dislocation involves
options: only minor stretching of a ligament with the joint surfaces remaining fully aligned
damage exclusively to skeletal muscle tissue with no joint involvement
the complete displacement of bone ends from their normal position within a joint, so that the articulating surfaces are no longer in proper contact
no pain, swelling, or loss of function whatsoever
questions.explanation: A dislocation occurs when the bones forming a joint are forced out of their normal alignment so the articulating surfaces are no longer properly in contact, which is more severe than the ligament stretching seen in a sprain.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The R.I.C.E. protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) is the recommended immediate first-aid management specifically for
options: severe open fractures requiring surgical intervention only
cardiac arrest, in place of CPR
choking, in place of the Heimlich manoeuvre
acute soft-tissue injuries such as sprains and strains, to limit swelling and control pain in the initial hours after injury
questions.explanation: R.I.C.E. -- Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation -- is the standard immediate first-aid approach for acute soft-tissue injuries like sprains and strains, aimed at minimising swelling and pain in the first 24-72 hours.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: When performing adult CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) according to widely taught guidelines, the recommended ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths for a single rescuer is generally
options: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
15 compressions to 1 breath
5 compressions to 5 breaths
50 compressions to 10 breaths
questions.explanation: Standard adult CPR guidelines for a single rescuer recommend cycles of 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, repeated until help arrives or the person recovers.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The recovery position, taught in basic first aid, is primarily used for an unconscious but breathing casualty in order to
options: restrain the casualty from any movement whatsoever
keep the airway open and reduce the risk of choking on vomit or the tongue obstructing the throat while awaiting further help
perform chest compressions more effectively
stimulate the casualty back into full consciousness immediately
questions.explanation: The recovery position keeps an unconscious, breathing casualty's airway clear, reducing the risk of choking on vomit or airway obstruction by the tongue, while medical help is awaited.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: The Heimlich manoeuvre (abdominal thrusts) is a first-aid technique specifically used to treat a person who is
options: experiencing a cardiac arrest with no pulse
suffering a simple ankle sprain
choking, with a foreign object obstructing their airway
experiencing a nosebleed
questions.explanation: The Heimlich manoeuvre uses forceful abdominal thrusts to dislodge a foreign object obstructing a choking person's airway, restoring normal breathing.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following correctly groups diseases according to their principal mode of transmission: malaria as vector-borne, tuberculosis as airborne, and cholera as waterborne?
options: Malaria is spread by airborne droplets, tuberculosis by mosquito vectors, and cholera by direct skin contact
All three diseases are transmitted exclusively through contaminated water sources
All three diseases share an identical mode of transmission via mosquito vectors

Malaria is transmitted via the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito (vector-borne), tuberculosis primarily via airborne respiratory droplets, and cholera primarily via contaminated water or food
questions.explanation: Malaria is a vector-borne disease transmitted by infected Anopheles mosquitoes, tuberculosis spreads mainly via airborne respiratory droplets, and cholera is primarily a waterborne disease spread through contaminated water or food.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Sickle cell anaemia, a genetically inherited condition prevalent in Nigeria, follows a recessive inheritance pattern such that two parents who are both carriers (genotype AS) have, on average, what probability of producing a child with the full disease genotype (SS)?
options: Approximately 25 percent (1 in 4) probability for each pregnancy
Zero probability; carriers can never have an affected child
Approximately 50 percent (1 in 2) probability for each pregnancy
100 percent probability for each pregnancy
questions.explanation: When both parents are AS carriers, Mendelian inheritance predicts an average of 25% AA (normal), 50% AS (carrier), and 25% SS (affected) offspring for each pregnancy, though outcomes vary randomly per individual pregnancy.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes a communicable disease from a non-communicable disease in terms of underlying cause?
options: Both types of disease are always caused by transmissible pathogens

A communicable disease is caused by a transmissible pathogen (such as a virus, bacterium, or parasite) and can spread between individuals, whereas a non-communicable disease typically arises from genetic, lifestyle, or environmental factors and does not spread person-to-person
Non-communicable diseases are always more contagious than communicable diseases
There is no meaningful distinction between the two categories
questions.explanation: Communicable diseases result from pathogens capable of transmission between individuals, whereas non-communicable diseases (such as hypertension, diabetes, or cancer) generally result from genetic, lifestyle, or environmental factors and do not spread from person to person.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Immunisation (vaccination) serves as a key public health strategy against communicable diseases mainly because it
options: directly cures an existing active infection instantly
eliminates the need for any other hygiene or sanitation practices
stimulates the immune system to develop protective antibodies in advance, reducing the likelihood or severity of future infection by a specific pathogen
is effective only against non-communicable diseases
questions.explanation: Vaccination primes the immune system to recognise and respond rapidly to a specific pathogen, reducing the likelihood of infection or the severity of disease upon future exposure.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Air pollution from vehicle exhaust and industrial emissions is a significant public health concern chiefly because it can
options: have no measurable effect on human respiratory or cardiovascular health
only affect plant life with no impact on human beings
improve overall air quality by increasing oxygen concentration
contribute to respiratory diseases, cardiovascular problems, and long-term environmental harm such as acid rain and climate change
questions.explanation: Air pollution from vehicle and industrial emissions contributes to respiratory and cardiovascular disease in humans and drives broader environmental harms such as acid rain and climate change.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Hypertension, a major non-communicable disease risk factor, is generally defined by which of the following blood pressure characteristics?
options: A persistently elevated arterial blood pressure, generally considered to be at or above 140/90 mmHg on repeated measurement
A persistently and abnormally low arterial blood pressure reading
A blood pressure reading that fluctuates only during vigorous exercise and never at rest
A condition defined exclusively by an abnormal heart rate with no reference to blood pressure
questions.explanation: Hypertension is characterised by a persistently elevated arterial blood pressure, conventionally defined as readings at or above 140/90 mmHg on repeated measurement, increasing risk for stroke and heart disease.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, a significant non-communicable disease, is primarily characterised by
options: the complete absence of insulin production from birth
insulin resistance and/or relative insulin deficiency, leading to chronically elevated blood glucose levels
an excessively low blood glucose level that resolves without treatment
a disease exclusively affecting the respiratory system
questions.explanation: Type 2 diabetes typically involves insulin resistance in body tissues combined with a relative deficiency in insulin production, resulting in chronically elevated blood glucose levels.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa are both classified as eating disorders, but they are distinguished from one another chiefly by the fact that bulimia typically involves
options: a total, sustained refusal to eat any food whatsoever with no binge-eating episodes
no psychological component at all, unlike anorexia

recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviours such as self-induced vomiting, whereas anorexia is characterised primarily by severe self-imposed food restriction and an intense fear of weight gain
exclusively affecting male athletes and never female athletes
questions.explanation: Bulimia nervosa is characterised by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviours (such as vomiting or excessive exercise), while anorexia nervosa centres on severe voluntary food restriction driven by an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the appropriate first-aid management of a suspected fracture at the scene of a sports injury, prior to professional medical care?
options: Forcefully realign the bone into its normal anatomical position immediately
Encourage the casualty to continue playing to 'walk it off'
Apply vigorous massage directly to the suspected fracture site
Immobilise the injured limb in the position found using an improvised splint, avoiding unnecessary movement, and seek urgent medical attention
questions.explanation: Correct first-aid management for a suspected fracture involves immobilising the limb as found, using a splint if available, avoiding unnecessary movement of the injured area, and arranging urgent medical attention -- never attempting to realign the bone.
